title: Building the confidence to grow: 3 opportunities for Sage partners
snippet: Three days in Amsterdam. One connected partner community. Practical ideas to help customers embrace change and unlock growth. The post Building the confidence to grow: 3 opportunities for Sage partners appeared first on Sage Advice UK.
fullText:
Key takeaways

Start with customer challenges, not technology: Identify where AI, automation and connected solutions can improve everyday business processes.

Build stronger advisory relationships: Help customers modernise their systems, adopt new capabilities and make better business decisions.

Look for opportunities to connect financial workflows: Integrated banking, payments and accounting can help reduce complexity and create new opportunities for partner services.

At Sage Future for Partners EMEA, partners from across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia Pacific came together in Amsterdam to explore a shared challenge: how to help customers grow confidently as technology and business expectations change.

Across three days of keynotes, demonstrations and discussions, the focus was on turning innovation into practical outcomes, and we discuss these now, as follows:

How can Sage partners turn innovation into customer value?

See the video above for a catch-up of the event, but for partners, it became clear that three opportunities stood out.

1. Help customers find practical uses for AI

AI can help businesses automate routine tasks, improve decision-making and work more efficiently. But customers need guidance on where to start.

Sessions exploring Sage AI, Sage X3 and Sage Intacct highlighted how partners can help customers identify valuable use cases and adopt new capabilities with confidence, giving them clarity on how decisions are made, control over what AI is doing, and accountability through a complete audit trail.

Start by identifying one time-consuming customer workflow and exploring whether AI or automation could simplify it. Focus on the business outcome rather than the technology itself.

2. Move from implementation to ongoing advice

As customers modernise their systems, partners have opportunities to offer more than technical implementation.

The event explored how industry expertise, cloud migration and advisory-led services can help partners build stronger customer relationships.

Review where existing customers could benefit from modernisation, then identify opportunities to support them beyond the initial implementation.

3. Explore opportunities in connected financial services

Businesses often manage banking, payments and accounting across separate systems, creating additional administration.

At Amsterdam, Sage announced partnerships with Adyen and Mastercard as it develops integrated financial services for small businesses, with the first implementation planned for France.

As Derk Bleeker, Chief Commercial Officer at Sage, said in the announcement: “Small businesses shouldn’t have to move between separate systems to manage their finances.”

Ask customers where disconnected financial tools create extra work. Understanding these challenges can help partners identify opportunities for more connected solutions as new capabilities become available.

Final thoughts: Turning ideas into action

The opportunity for partners is to turn innovation into practical customer outcomes, whether through AI, advisory services or more connected financial workflows.

But growth also depends on collaboration. By sharing expertise, strengthening relationships and working together across the Sage partner community, partners can create new opportunities for their businesses and help customers grow with confidence.

Thank you to everyone who joined us in Amsterdam. We look forward to building on these conversations and growing together.
